text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'resv-west-2-gpu' crossing capacity threshold — 100% reserved GPU utilization. Queue length spiking from 1.2k -> 3.1k in last 10m. Multiple tenants impacted, highest priority: AtlasCorp (enterprise). Trigger: autoscaler hit max_instances. Paging oncall-maya.
oncall-maya: @here getting the page, jumping in. Observed increased 503s on /v1/generate for AtlasCorp routes. Any immediate mitigation suggestions? :rotating_light:
sre-omar: I'm looking at metrics. Autoscaler logs show scale failure: "Reached max_nodes limit (12)" and repeated scale attempts 04:12-04:18 UTC. Also several eviction events for best-effort sessions.
eng-li: Confirmed — scheduler refused new allocations; also noisy_sessions metric for tenant 'vendor-x' high. Looks like one tenant is holding many long-lived sessions with big KV caches.
prod-carmen: Customer impact: AtlasCorp reporting elevated error rates and long queue times, internal SLOs are breached. Account team notified. acct-rye: I'm on the customer bridge with AtlasCorp; they're seeing timeouts and are asking for ETA.
sre-omar: Quick mitigation plan: 1) enable routing fallback for AtlasCorp to hosted fallback pool (lower perf) 2) run targeted preemptive eviction on noisy sessions 3) temporarily increase autoscaler max_nodes if cloud quota allows. Which order?
oncall-maya: Do 1 then 2. Hosted fallback minimizes customer impact immediately. I'll spin up the fallback route.
eng-li: Routing flag applied: set route atlascorp->fallback-west with model_variant=gpt-small-quant, weight=100. Propagation logs: 
```
PUT /routes/atlascorp
{ "fallback": "hosted-west", "variant": "gpt-small-quant" }
200 OK
```
ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK STEP: fallback routing applied. Next: eviction script option: `scripts/evict_noisy.sh --pool resv-west-2-gpu --threshold 0.5`
sre-omar: Preparing eviction dry-run to list candidate sessions first. Running: 
```
./scripts/list_long_kv_sessions --pool resv-west-2-gpu --limit 100
# output columns: session_id, tenant, kv_mb, last_active
# sample:
# s-9a3f, vendor-x, 18432MB, 2024-12-05T04:05:12Z
# s-0b2d, atlascorp, 1024MB, 2024-12-05T04:14:44Z
```
eng-li: Most heavy KV sessions belong to vendor-x (not AtlasCorp). They have many pinned long-lived chats. I'd recommend targeting vendor-x first for evictions and throttle their new session creation.
custops-jun: If we evict vendor-x sessions, will they lose progress? They are internal to that tenant; we need to notify them. cc @acct-rye for outreach.
acct-rye: I'll ping vendor-x contacts; we should give 2 min notice before forced evict. Sending message now.
eng-li: Starting eviction: 
```
./scripts/evict_noisy.sh --pool resv-west-2-gpu --tenant vendor-x --grace 120
# triggered at 04:22:12 UTC
```
sre-omar: Eviction running. Early results: reclaimed ~38 GPUs worth of KV memory by dropping 220 sessions. Queue length fell 3.1k -> 1.1k over 5m. Latency for AtlasCorp improved slightly.
oncall-maya: Can we also temporarily bump autoscaler max to 16? Cloud quotas may allow +4. I'm ready to request quota bump.
prod-carmen: We should only do autoscaler bump if eviction doesn't stabilize queue for AtlasCorp. Risk: cost and possibly enabling noisy tenant to occupy more.
eng-li: I'm enabling session creation throttle for vendor-x: allowed_new_sessions=1/min and reduced KV cache retention for their sessions. Patch applied.
ops-runbook-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: throttle applied to tenant vendor-x. Monitor for retry storms.
sre-omar: Metrics update: queue 1.1k -> 430 in next 8m. AtlasCorp error rate down from 18% -> 3%. Good sign.
acct-rye: Vendor-x acknowledged eviction and accepted temporary throttle. They're cooperating. AtlasCorp on the bridge reports requests succeeding again.
eng-li: Decided to postpone autoscaler bump for now. We'll keep fallback route active for AtlasCorp for 60m and monitor. I'm also adding a short-lived admission control rule: reserve_atlas_priority=high to avoid further migrations.
oncall-maya: I'm handing off to day shift SRE lead @sre-omar for follow-up and postmortem. Creating incident channel and pager note.
sre-omar: Taking over. Immediate action list captured in incident doc: - Confirmed root cause: long-lived KV-heavy sessions from vendor-x causing noisy-neighbor resource pressure + autoscaler hitting configured max_nodes. - Mitigations: eviction + throttle + customer fallback routing. - Next steps: follow-up with infra to consider autoscaler policy change (dynamic max based on short-term spike), add per-tenant KV caps, and surface tenant usage into billing alerts.
prod-carmen: I'll draft customer-facing summary for AtlasCorp and coordinate comms with acct-rye. Add note to postmortem: faster per-tenant soft-limits.
acct-rye: For AtlasCorp comms: ETA recovery communicated as ~10-15m; they appreciate quick response. I'll follow-up w/ formal update in 30m.
ops-runbook-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: created incident/2024-12-05-resv-west-2-exhaustion, assigned to sre-omar.
sre-omar: Logging final metrics snapshot before close: 
```
time: 2024-12-05T05:10:00Z
pool: resv-west-2-gpu
utilization: 68%
queue_length: 72
atlascorp_error_rate: 0.8%
vendor-x_new_session_rate: 0.02/s (throttled)
```
custops-jun: Marking customer impact: AtlasCorp degraded for ~22 minutes, partial timeout for high-concurrency routes. No data loss reported.
oncall-maya: Great job team. Leaving follow-up tasks for postmortem. Closing oncall page. :white_check_mark:
